trivia: Did you know? The first computer network was the ARPANET, launched in 1969!
Fun fact: The first ever email was sent by Ray Tomlinson in 1971!
Networking trivia: IPv6 has 340 undecillion addresses—enough to give every grain of sand its own IP!
Cisco was founded in 1984 by a married couple from Stanford who just wanted to email each other from different buildings.
The name 'Cisco' comes from San Francisco—look closely at the logo and you’ll see the Golden Gate Bridge.
The first Cisco product was a router that ran a hacked version of Stanford’s software.
Cisco’s first customer was a local area network at Stanford University.
The original Cisco router was built from parts ordered by mail and assembled by hand in a living room.
In 2000, Cisco briefly became the most valuable company in the world—surpassing Microsoft at the time.
The CCIE (Cisco Certified Internetwork Expert) is one of the most respected certifications in IT.
The CCIE lab exam originally included physical cabling you had to patch manually!
Fun fact: Cisco acquired over 200 companies to expand its product portfolio—from Meraki to Webex.
Cisco’s stock symbol is CSCO because the ticker 'CISCO' was already taken by a food company.
Cisco’s early slogan was 'The Human Network'—emphasizing the people behind the technology.
Cisco’s first acquisition was Crescendo Communications in 1993—marking its entry into the switching market.
The 'Catalyst' switch line came from the Crescendo acquisition—and it lives on today.
In 2010, Cisco introduced TelePresence—a video conferencing system so clear it was used for remote medical consultations.
Cisco’s ASA firewalls once ran a game of Lunar Lander as an Easter egg in debug mode.
Cisco was one of the first major vendors to invest in SDN—software-defined networking—with the ACI platform.
During the COVID-19 pandemic, Cisco's Webex saw a 600% increase in usage almost overnight.
